result.title: Single-Image Food Mass Estimators Do Not Transfer Their Gram Scale Across Datasets
result.comment: 19 pages, 6 figures, 13 tables. Code, set lists and model weights: https://github.com/yongshenglian/foodmass-transfer
result.summary: Estimating food mass from a photograph is central to image-based dietary assessment, but whether trained models transfer to new cameras and foods is unclear. We fine-tuned DINOv2-base on 2,253 weighed Nutrition5k dishes to predict mass from one RGB photograph and compared it with a zero-shot vision-language model, Qwen3-VL-32B, on Nutrition5k and three external datasets: ASA24 studio portions, ECUSTFD whole foods and Food Portion Benchmark meal trays. In domain, the fine-tuned model's mean absolute error was 24.8 g, less than half of Qwen's. On external datasets it did not beat Qwen. For a food it had never seen, it ranked portions by size, but no better than a count of food pixels. Its gram scale was wrong in two ways: it changed with how much of the scene the photograph showed, and it was off by a different factor for each food. Training on other foods or trays from the tested dataset cut the external error by 38 to 65%. DINOv2-large, a larger backbone trained on the same dishes, did not reduce the external error. One labeled photograph of the same food cut the model's ASA24 error to 28.3 g, better than that photograph achieved alone. Prediction intervals that held the true mass for 90% of Nutrition5k dishes held it for at most half of external photographs. Nutrition5k often photographed the same plate several times, so a random test split shared near-identical photographs with training and overstated accuracy. Single-image mass estimators therefore need labeled photographs from the setting where they are used.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Nutrition5k 上微调 DINOv2-base 做单张 RGB 图像的食物质量回归，并与零样本 Qwen3-VL-32B 在三个外部数据集上比较，分析跨域迁移失败、误差来源（视野范围、按食物类型成比例的尺度偏差）及预测区间校准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不优于食物像素计数」的基线、按食物类别成比例的尺度误差与跨域预测区间失效，可供核查模型是否真正利用定量视觉证据、latent 状态是否保留任务必要几何信息；但与 latent 推理机制无直接关系，仅提供诊断视角。
